Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test is `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.CoreOperationTest.testNodeSetOperations()`. The test includes the assertion `assertXPathValue(context, "$array > 0", Boolean.TRUE, Boolean.class);` which is designed to test comparison between a node-set (an XPath array variable) and a number (0). According to the XPath specification quoted in the bug report, when comparing a node-set to a number with operators like `>`, the comparison should be true if there exists any node in the node-set such that the numeric comparison with that number is true.

The bug report states that binary operators behavior involving node-sets is incorrect, specifically that the current implementation does not adhere to the XPath specification for comparing two node-sets or a node-set and a number. This suggests that the logic handling binary operations in such cases is likely flawed.

Since the test fails on evaluating an expression involving `"$array > 0"`, it implies that the code responsible for evaluating binary operations has incorrect handling of node-sets when compared with numbers or other node-sets. The method that performs the binary operation evaluation is likely responsible, but the exact method name in `CoreOperation` for evaluation or computation related to binary operators was not found (`computeValue` exists but is abstract).

The root cause is the mishandling (incorrect boolean result) of comparisons involving node-sets in the binary operation evaluation logic, where it should iterate through the nodes and compare their string-values per the XPath spec. The bug manifests as failed test assertions that expect a true comparison when a node's value satisfies the comparison, but the code does not yield true as expected.

Given the test and description, the bug is likely found in the binary operator evaluation logic in the compiler component that evaluates XPath expressions involving node-sets and scalar values.

Next, it would be useful to examine any concrete subclasses of `CoreOperation` that implement `computeValue` or any helper methods handling node-set to number or node-set to node-set comparisons within binary operations. This will localize the incorrect behavior within the implementation.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
